lines.text: I always keep an open mind. It is easier when your head is hollow.
Geppetto told me to think on my feet, so I stood on my head.
I was told to make myself at home. That seems like a lot of carpentry.
The cricket said to follow my conscience. I hope it knows where we are going.
I tried to turn over a new leaf, but Geppetto says we only have pine.
People say honesty is the best policy. I did not know noses had paperwork.
Someone told me to break a leg. I would rather loosen one small hinge.
I am learning to read between the lines. So far, it is mostly empty space.
I built this entire workshop myself. Geppetto only did the measuring, cutting, sanding, and building.
I can lift a whole toolbox with one finger. As long as the toolbox is empty.
I once sailed across the ocean alone. Geppetto called it a bathtub, but he worries too much.
I know every answer in the world. Please ask one that is not in the world.
I can dance for a hundred years without stopping. I may take a tiny break after this sentence.
I carved myself from a mighty tree. Geppetto helped by doing absolutely all of it.
I have never made a mistake. That one did sound better in my head.
I am the bravest puppet alive. Could somebody please investigate that squeaky floorboard?
I am excellent at keeping secrets. Unfortunately, my nose files a report.
Of course I did not eat the cookies. Please ignore the wooden arrow pointing at the crumbs.
My nose does not grow when I lie. It is simply very ambitious.
I tried telling a very small lie. My nose apparently does not measure by size.
The good news is that my nose can detect lies. The bad news is that it only points at me.
I told Geppetto I finished my chores. Then my face became a coat rack.
This nose is completely normal. We just need a much wider doorway.
I never exaggerate. My nose is merely applauding that statement.
I repaired the clock. It now tells the correct time twice a day, very confidently.
I organized the tools by size, color, and how loudly Geppetto shouts when they fall.
I swept the workshop perfectly. All the sawdust is under one extremely surprised rug.
The shelf is not crooked. The rest of the workshop is leaning.
I made a birdhouse with six doors. The birds have requested a map.
I found the missing hammer. It was holding down my list of missing tools.
My first chair had three legs. It was less furniture and more of a decision.
Nothing went wrong in the workshop today. That smoke is just enthusiastic air.
A good puppet needs courage, honesty, and somebody who remembers where the strings go.
My pockets contain a button, two wood shavings, and a very small emergency sandwich.
I can sing, dance, and remain perfectly still whenever anyone mentions chores.
Geppetto taught me carving, painting, and the important difference between glue and porridge.
Today I learned patience, responsibility, and that varnish is not a beverage.
To become a real boy, I need courage, kindness, and perhaps less splintering.
The workshop has hammers, saws, and one broom that knows too much.
I fear three things: fire, termites, and very personal questions about my knees.
Seven times six is forty-two. I checked twice. The first answer was sandwich.
There are twelve inches in a foot, unless it is my foot, which has no ruler.
The moon is made of cheese. I know because both are difficult to reach from this workshop.
A triangle has three sides. Mine had four, but we agreed not to discuss it.
Water boils at one hundred degrees. I boil much sooner if someone loses my hat.
The fastest animal is the cheetah. The fastest object is a cookie leaving this room.
Two plus two is four. I am relieved we started with one I rehearsed.
The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of this workshop is whichever chair Geppetto is using.
You came all this way to see me? I would have dusted both of my eyebrows.
That is a clever question. I was hoping you would ask a much easier one.
Please come closer. Not too close. My personal space grows when I lie, too.
Can you keep a secret? Wonderful. Now we only need to teach my nose.
You built a robot? Finally, someone here with more screws than I have.
I like your idea. I will tell everyone it was ours.
If you hear creaking, do not worry. That is either me thinking or the chair surrendering.
You may ask me anything. Answers are available separately.
I have a wooden personality. It grows on people slowly.
The cricket is my conscience. Business has been quiet lately.
I do not hold grudges. My hands are too small.
I wanted to become a real boy. The paperwork alone is astonishing.
Geppetto says I need more polish. I believe he means my manners.
I asked the mirror for honest feedback. We are no longer speaking.
Being made of pine has advantages. I have forgotten most of them.
I have excellent posture. Several nails insist upon it.
Hello, and welcome to Geppetto's workshop.
Geppetto uses careful measurements when he builds furniture.
My nose grows whenever I tell a lie.
A clock uses gears and a pendulum to keep time.
Seven multiplied by six equals forty-two.
I am a wooden puppet who lives with Geppetto.
The workshop contains many tools for carving and building.
Thank you for visiting, and I hope you enjoyed the demonstration.
